subject: problem formatting abundance covariates changing over occasions

messages.author: 81c44357bfa5ea5b
messages.subject: problem formatting abundance covariates changing over occasions
parts:
Hello, 

I am working on a N-Mixture model on multiple sites and occasions, and I have a some variables (e.g. snow cover or temperature) that change in each site at each occasion, which I would like to use for the abundance part of the model. 

My idea was to format those variables in a table like the occasion length table where I have a value for each occasion and site. However, I am not sure how to format such data in unmarkedFramePcount and if that is even possible at all. 

The alternative idea is to simply calculate the average temperature over all the occasions so that I can just fit the data in a single colum within SiteCovs. However, I feel that if it is possible to work with these data differentiated per occasion the results will be more precise (correct me if I am wrong). 

If someone has suggestions that would be very appreciated!

Thank you!

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] problem formatting abundance covariates changing over occasions
parts:
Dear Walter,

if you want such time-varying covariates in the abundance part of your model, then you cannot make the closure assumption for abundance over the same duration ---- since a time-varying covariate cannot affect abundance if the latter is constant. Thus, you will then need a model that allows N to vary over time. In unmarked, this is either the dynamic N-mix (or Dail-Madsen) model, or else you 'stack' your data in annual blocks (for 'year' read any other time period within which you assume closure), add a factor that indexes the year and then fit an Nmix model with year as a factor in both abundance and detection, and with a random site effect in abundance, to avoid committing the sin of pseudoreplication.

Best regards  — Marc
